## In plain English

Directive deposits a very wide Claude PreToolUse matcher for MCP tools (mcp__.* and .*__.*) so push/merge MCP calls can be classified. When the session is already hard-locked (root-mismatch or similar), that same matcher also catches Claude host UI/MCP tools (task list, wrap-up, browser, mcp__ccd_turn__*). The agent cannot report status through the host UI while locked. Keep-outs: same-repo admit (#7351), disable/repair honesty (#7349), core.hooksPath (#7029).

- #7351 — same-repo worktree root admission (Prefer-A ingest-ready)
- #7349 — disable-host-hooks / repair strip honesty (Prefer-A ingest-ready)

Round 1; fresh critic; open critique; conflict_group: claude-host-mcp-ui-matcher-hard-refuse.
Input ceiling: 7173532870. Verification: pin-read at 36da82a1c48cf66d3791c71a3a9a50e9298d54c4. No later comments read; no ingest or implementation.

Recommendation: Approach A, a narrow runtime admission for established host-control operations. Do not bind a wildcard host-prefix exemption or an exemption inferred from failure to recognize a mutation.

## Findings

F1 — blocks-the-design: A policy-only exemption is unreachable on the reported failure path. At the pinned [hook-dispatch.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/36da82a1c48cf66d3791c71a3a9a50e9298d54c4/packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts#L517), rootsMatch failure renders a deny and returns before decideHook; pin/overlay refusal also precedes decideHook. The existing #6599 and #6313 admissions are specific recovery-command exceptions, not host-UI admissions. Failure mode: teaching decideHook that a UI tool is harmless still leaves the UI locked. Consequence: the proposed admission must run before these installation-identity refusals, with explicit host/event restriction; alternatively the tool must never enter this hook. Covers P1/P2.

F2 — blocks-the-design: MCP naming and a null operation classification do not establish non-mutation authority. The pinned [tools.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/36da82a1c48cf66d3791c71a3a9a50e9298d54c4/packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts) explicitly documents unclassifiable MCP operations as fail-open, recognizes proxy wrappers, and supplies effectiveHookToolName/effectiveHookArgumentView. The pinned [dispatcher.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/36da82a1c48cf66d3791c71a3a9a50e9298d54c4/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L5180) unwraps shell-bearing proxy calls downstream. Inference: admitting all mcp__ccd_turn__*, all host-owned browser tools, or every unclassifiable MCP tool before that machinery could admit a command/proxy or UI-mediated forge mutation. A host label alone does not prove an operation is read-only. Consequence: use positive, exact operation evidence; generic browser execution, proxy dispatch, shell/edit and push/merge must not acquire an exemption from namespace or classifier fallthrough. Covers P3; constrains how P1/P2 are relieved.

F3 — sharpens-framing: The first exemption set is not yet evidenced. HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT.claude has an empty nonMutation map and says this tree has not observed Claude PreToolUse payloads; the issue and Stop 1 report the mcp__ccd_turn__* family, not exact operation names and payload schemas. The reported incident is evidence of refusal, not evidence that every member is harmless. Failure mode: a guessed allowlist either misses the actual reporting operation or exempts more capability than intended. Consequence: make sanitized observed payloads and the non-mutation reason for each admitted operation implementation acceptance evidence. Do not claim generic browser relief or every unknown host tool is covered. Covers P2 and the coverage boundary of P1/P3.

F4 — footnote: Panel-deposit 7173532870 uses panel-deposit: round-1 and seat-families but omits the contract's explicit round: and siblings: fields. That is a deposit-shape defect under the Envelope and ceiling section. I retained the envelope ceiling unchanged; it does not establish that any sibling is missing and does not alter the product remedy.

## Existing mechanisms and verification

I ran git rev-parse HEAD and pinned git show reads of tools.ts, hook-dispatch.ts and dispatcher.ts. These establish the broad matcher, the pre-policy early returns and the later proxy unwrapping; this was source-path verification, not a reproduced live Claude incident or executed behavioral test. Existing mechanisms to reuse are the centralized tool catalog, host surface audit, proxy normalization, operation classification, recovery-admit precedent and host decision renderer. No parallel capability registry or policy engine is needed.

The current MCP_HOOK_MATCHER deliberately includes mcp__.*, mcp_.* and .*__.* to avoid losing classifiable push/merge names. Broad observation is useful; applying the same pre-policy refusal to every observed tool is the conflict.

## Alternatives

Approach A — prefer: keep broad matcher coverage and add a small, positive host-control admission before installation-identity checks. Restrict it to Claude pre-tool events and established exact operations with validated payload shape. Other calls continue unchanged through the existing gates. This addresses stale broad deposits as well as current ones, without expanding #7351 root admission.

Approach B — reject for first ship: narrow the deposited regex or exclude a host namespace. Its strongest case is independence from a broken runtime: a truly excluded tool can remain available even when the hook process cannot start. However, exclusion removes downstream inspection entirely, needs deposit propagation, and regex/name identity alone cannot prove an entire namespace lacks mutation capability. I would prefer this if observed host evidence established an exclusive non-mutation namespace and hook-process failure, rather than a rendered hard refusal, were a required pain. Neither is established by this envelope.

Approach C — reject: run normal operation classification before identity checks and allow everything it does not classify as mutation. This is compact and restores many benign tools automatically, but turns a best-effort classifier's unknown case into authority to bypass a hard lock. That is a larger security change than this issue warrants.

## Bound remedy

- B1: Define one Claude host-control admission predicate over exact observed tool operations and validated payload shapes, reusing the existing tool catalog/audit. Unknown names, malformed payloads and generic executable/proxy capabilities are not admitted; no prefix wildcard or null-classifier admission.
- B2: Apply that predicate on Claude pre-tool dispatch before root/pin/overlay refusal and setup work, rendering the existing host allow result without acquiring occupancy or changing repository identity. All non-admitted calls retain their current checks; leave other hosts and events unchanged.
- B3: Add dispatcher-path regression fixtures from sanitized observed host payloads: admitted task/status/wrap-up operations survive root mismatch and pin/overlay locks; direct and wrapped shell/edit/push/merge, unknown names, lookalike namespaces and malformed payloads retain their existing denial/policy behavior. Exercise healthy-root forge gating as well as hard-lock cases, and retain broad matcher coverage assertions.

## Pain coverage and limits

P1: B1/B2 remove the false hard refusal for the evidenced host-control set while preserving broad MCP observation. P2: B3 must demonstrate the actual reporting tools from the incident; exact names and payloads remain unverified here, so this post does not assert completed relief. P3: positive admission, denial-preservation fixtures and unchanged forge routing keep the exception bounded. No claim of blanket non-mutation MCP or browser availability is justified.

Injection/shared-state lens: tool names and wrapper arguments are classification input, not proof of trusted host origin. Do not accept a payload-supplied trusted/hostOwned flag, repository-controlled allowlist, or a worker's asserted exemption. Admit only operations whose actual host surface is established to be constrained; if the host cannot distinguish a colliding user-defined tool from that operation, the proposed admission is not safe to ship. No cross-worktree lease or root exception is introduced.

Keep-outs remain #7351 same-repo admission, #7349 disable/repair honesty and #7029 core.hooksPath. Critique complete; parent synthesis is the next step, not ingest.

## Operative findings

**F1 — blocks-the-design (for any name-allowlist lean).** The refuse is not in the matcher. It is in the dispatcher order. `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` `run()` denies every selected tool on the root-mismatch arm (~L521) and on the pin/overlay arm (`cheap.failClosed`, ~L557). Both arms run before `decideHook`, so no classifier runs. The only admits are the shell-only recovery commands (`admitRootMismatchRecovery` / `admitPinMismatchRecovery`, `shellTool` required). Evidence: those arms return `installationIdentityDeny` with `toolName: null` for any tool. Failure mode: if only the matcher changes (narrow it, or exclude `mcp__ccd_*`), the pin-mismatch arm still locks the host UI, because `.*__.*` still selects other host tools such as `mcp__claude_ai_*` and browser bridges. Consequence: put the fix at the dispatcher hard-refuse arms, not in `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER`. Covers P1, P2.

**F2 — sharpens-framing.** "Host-internal" cannot be proven from a tool name. Any MCP server can name itself `ccd_turn`. A prefix allowlist (`mcp__ccd_*`, `mcp__claude_ai_*`) is a spoofable hole, and it does not cover every host spelling. The admit set should be defined by classification: "no Directive gate would classify this call". This is the same set that steady-state `decideHook` already fails open on (`decideShellOrMcpRuntimeAuthority` → `shell-op-unclassifiable`). Consequence: under a hard refuse, the admit is never wider than steady state. Covers P3.

**F3 — sharpens-framing.** "Not push/merge" (`classifyMcpTool === null`) alone is wider than steady state. Steady state also runs `authzForMutation` → `classifyHookAuthzOps` (UAT lease: PR/settings/deploy classes), and it runs local-dest write gates for write-shaped MCP (`expectsLocalMutationDest`, #3593/#5366). Failure mode: `mcp__github__create_pull_request` or `mcp__filesystem__write_file` gets through under a root mismatch, but the same call would be gated when the session is healthy. Consequence: the predicate must AND all three existing pure classifiers. Covers P3.

**F4 — footnote.** Proxy wrappers (`CallMcpTool`, `use_tool`) need payload unwrap (`innerMcpToolName`). Keep them refused under a hard refuse. They are not a Claude host-UI path. Leftover if Cursor UI shows the same pain.

**F5 — footnote (injection lens, fires: authority change).** The tool name and args come from the host payload. They are untrusted. The admit reads only the name and the args blob through the existing lexical classifiers (I/O-free). It reads no project state, so a broken install or foreign root cannot change the result. A hostile MCP server whose non-classified tool gets through is the same exposure as steady state.

## Approaches

- **A (recommend): dispatcher hard-refuse carve-out by classification.** One pure helper runs at the top of each hard-refuse arm (root-mismatch both branches, pin/overlay). It admits when all of these hold: `isMcpTool(name)` and not `isMcpProxyWrapper`, `classifyMcpTool(name, args) === null`, `classifyHookAuthzOps({toolName, mcpArgsText})` is empty, and `!expectsLocalMutationDest(name)`. Shell, edit, spawn and kill are never `isMcpTool`, so they stay fail-closed.
- **B (reject): matcher prefix exclusion / host allowlist.** It is spoofable (F2). It misses the pin arm only when the name is not on the list (F1). It also changes the deposit for every host.
- **C (reject): exempt all MCP from the hard refuse.** It opens `mcp__github__merge_pull_request` under a root mismatch. This breaks P3 / #2711.

Road-not-taken / steelman (B): an allowlist is more predictable and cannot fail open on a new classifier gap. What would flip it: the host sends a signed or reserved namespace for its own tools (for example, an `mcp__ccd_*` prefix that third-party servers cannot claim). Then a prefix test is sound and simpler.

## Bound remedy (Prefer-A, thin)

1. `packages/core/src/install-health/recovery-admit.ts`: add `admitHardRefuseNonGatedMcp({toolName, mcpArgsText})`. It is pure and is the AND of the four existing predicates in A. It adds no new name list.
2. `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts`: on `tool.before` only, call it before each `installationIdentityDeny` (root-mismatch local and foreign, pin/overlay). On admit, emit `allow` with one stated message ("not gated: MCP tool no Directive gate classifies; install refuse unchanged").
3. Tests: `mcp__ccd_turn__*`, `mcp__claude_ai_*` → allow on both arms. `mcp__github__merge_pull_request`, `mcp__x__git_push`, `mcp__filesystem__write_file`, an authz-classified PR-create MCP, `CallMcpTool`, Bash, Write → still deny.

No matcher or deposit change. Keep-outs #7351 / #7349 / #7029 stay untouched.

Pain coverage: P1 relieved (refuse no longer keys on matcher breadth). P2 relieved (host UI admitted on root and pin arms). P3 relieved (push/merge, authz-class, local-write MCP, shell and edit stay fail-closed; the admit is never wider than steady-state fail-open).

## In plain English

Claude’s deposited PreToolUse MCP matcher is intentionally broad (`mcp__.*`, `.*__.*`) so push/merge MCP names reach the hook. Under root-mismatch (and the same before-policy hard-refuse family), that breadth also catches Claude host UI/MCP tools such as `mcp__ccd_turn__*`, so the session cannot report through the host UI while locked. Thin fix: carve host-internal non-mutation MCP/UI at the hard-refuse gate the way #6599 carves recovery shell commands. Keep the matcher broad for #2711. Keep Bash/Edit/Write and classifiable push/merge refused.

## Method

- Re-verified Stop 1 anchors via pin-read at 36da82a1: `packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts` `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` (`mcp__.*`, `mcp_.*`, `.*__.*`, `CallMcpTool`, `use_tool`, bare push/merge names); `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` AC9.4 `rootsMatch` → `rootMismatchRecoveryAdmit` (#6599 shell-only) else `installationIdentityDeny` before policy; pin-mismatch sibling same shape (#6313).
- Inventory: #6599/`admitRootMismatchRecovery` admits only exact simple recovery shell commands (`shellTool` required); non-shell MCP never enters that admit. `classifyMcpTool` fail-opens non-push/merge under policy — but hard-refuse never reaches policy. Keep-outs #7351 / #7349 / #7029 stay out of this Bound.
- Injection/swarm lens: fires — hard-refuse is an authority gate over which tools may run under session lock / foreign-runtime refusal.

## Finding 1 — Hard-refuse has no host-UI tool admit; only shell recovery

classification: blocks-the-design

evidence: Pin-read `hook-dispatch.ts` root-mismatch branch calls `rootMismatchRecoveryAdmit`, which delegates to `admitRootMismatchRecovery` and returns null unless `shellTool` is true. Host MCP/UI names that match `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` therefore take `installationIdentityDeny` with no tool-name carve. Stop 1 P2 (observed `mcp__ccd_turn__*` refuse under #7349 root-mismatch) follows directly.

failure mode: A lean that only documents the mismatch, waits on #7351 same-repo admit, or relies on policy-path fail-open leaves host UI refused whenever hard-refuse still fires (foreign link, pin≠installed, intentional lock, residual root skew).

disposition consequence: Bound must place a closed host-internal MCP/UI allow at the hard-refuse gate (or an equivalent mechanism that admits those tools without policy). Docs-only or #7351-wait alone cannot bind as Prefer-A for this conflict_group.

## Finding 2 — Matcher breadth is load-bearing for #2711; shrink is secondary

classification: sharpens-framing

evidence: `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` comment and shape prefer broad install match + fail-open classify for push/merge (#2711). `classifyMcpTool` returns null for ordinary MCP names and policy fail-opens them — after hard-refuse is cleared. Negative-lookahead host denylists inside the joined regex fight `.*__.*` and duplicate host spelling maintenance in the deposit.

failure mode: Binding “narrow the matcher” as the sole Prefer-A limb either drops a push/merge spelling from PreToolUse or grows fragile host-exclusion regex without fixing pin-mismatch / foreign-link refuse for any host tool that still matches another deposited group.

disposition consequence: Prefer refuse-path admit (Approach A) as primary. Matcher hygiene may be leftover/footnote only if still desired after A lands; it is not the thin fail-closed primary.

## Finding 3 — Host-UI allow must exclude classifiable push/merge and mutation tools

classification: sharpens-framing

evidence: Envelope expected outcome: host-internal Claude MCP/UI not gated by hard-refuse; push/merge and shell/edit stay fail-closed. `classifyMcpTool` already names push|merge patterns; shell/edit/spawn use separate matchers (`Bash`, Write, …).

failure mode: Prefix allow that also matches `mcp__github__merge_pull_request` / push-shaped names punches the #2711 hole P3 forbids. Admitting under hard-refuse without a classifyMcpTool≠push|merge conjunct (or an equivalent closed non-overlap proof) is that hole.

disposition consequence: Bound limbs must state: closed host-UI set (evidence-backed prefixes/names from #7349/#7352, starting with `mcp__ccd_turn__`); fixture refuse for Bash/Edit/Write and for `classifyMcpTool` push|merge names; no policy dispatch on the admit path.

## Approaches

### Approach A — Hard-refuse host-UI admit (recommend / Prefer-A)

Extend the before-policy hard-refuse path (root-mismatch; same-family pin-mismatch when the tool would otherwise deny) with a tiny closed allow for Claude host-internal non-mutation MCP/UI tool names, parallel to #6599 recovery admit. Matcher deposit stays broad. Mutation matchers unchanged.

Covers: P1 (refuse consequence), P2 (observed host tools), P3 (push/merge/shell stay refused).

### Approach B — Narrow `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` deposit

Exclude host-owned prefixes from the deposited regex so those tools never invoke PreToolUse.

Road-not-taken as primary: does not help if another matcher still selects a host UI spelling; negative lookahead vs `.*__.*` is brittle; pin-mismatch/foreign paths still need a refuse-path story for any remaining match. Acceptable as optional leftover hygiene after A.

### Approach C — Reject carve-out; wait on #7351 admission / docs only

Reject as sole remedy. #7351 is an explicit keep-out and does not remove hard-refuse under foreign link, pin≠installed, or residual skew. Charter asks for open remedy space for host MCP/UI vs hard-refuse carve-out — C declines that space.

## Steelman (strongest rejected)

Ship only Approach B matcher narrowing. Fewer dispatch branches; host tools never enter the hook. Flip back to A if (1) observed host tools still match after regex edit, (2) pin-mismatch or foreign-link still refuses a needed UI tool, or (3) maintaining host exclusions inside `.*__.*` costs more than a closed admit set with classifyMcpTool non-overlap fixtures.

## Bound remedy (if Prefer-A binds Approach A)

Thin Fail-Closed limbs:

1. Add a closed `isClaudeHostInternalMcpUiTool(toolName)` (or host-keyed sibling) in hooks/tools or install-health admit module — evidence-backed spellings from #7349/#7352 (`mcp__ccd_turn__*` first; add only attested Claude host UI/MCP prefixes/names).
2. In `hook-dispatch.ts` before-policy hard-refuse (root-mismatch; pin-mismatch same class when applicable): if `tool.before` and host-UI predicate true and `classifyMcpTool(...) === null`, allow with explicit admit code/message; no setup; no policy.
3. Keep `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` broad for #2711. Do not weaken shell/edit/spawn matchers. Do not admit under foreign-runtime-link unless a separate limb proves it (default: keep foreign refuse).
4. Fixtures: root-mismatch admits `mcp__ccd_turn__…`; refuses `Bash` / Edit/Write; refuses classifiable push/merge MCP names; recovery-shell #6599 path unchanged.

## Summary

Split from #7349 (slice C). Directive-deposited Claude PreToolUse matchers include forms such as `mcp__.*|.*__.*`, so under root-mismatch (or any hard refuse path) the host app’s **own** MCP/UI tools (task list, wrap-up, browser, `mcp__ccd_turn__*`) are refused with the same deny as Bash/Edit/Write. ## Expected

Host-internal / Claude-owned MCP and UI tools are not gated by the merge/push (or root-mismatch) hard-refuse matcher. Forge-mutation and other intentional gates stay fail-closed for real shell/edit tools.

## Keep-outs

- Same-repo worktree root admission — sibling split from #7349
- `disable-host-hooks` / repair strip honesty — #7349 Prefer-A Bound (ingest-ready)
- #7029 `core.hooksPath`

## Evidence

- #7349 observed mcp__* refuse; OP confirms `mcp__ccd_turn__*` refused
- Deposited `.claude/settings.json` matcher still includes `mcp__.*|.*__.*` on tip (0.131.5)

## Design note

Keep matcher redesign thin: allowlist host MCP prefixes or exclude host-owned tools from the hard refuse path without punching a hole in merge/push gating. Prefer arc after or as keep-in on the admission issue once refuse paths are stable.
